query: For rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys intended for magnetic refrigeration, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields while maintaining rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability? State one controlled intervention that would test the hypothesis, the observations predicted relative to a baseline, the boundaries over which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence that would support it, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In rare-earth-free Fe–Mn–Co–Ni–Si high-entropy alloys (HEAs), a large, low-field magnetocaloric effect (MCE) together with fast heat exchange, low hysteresis and good mechanical strength is maximised when the alloy’s average valence-electron concentration (VEC) is tuned to ≈7.40 ± 0.05 e⁄atom, which brings the system to the verge of a first-order metamagnetic transition (paramagnetic bcc-like austenite → ferromagnetic bct-like martensite). Nanoscale (5–20 nm) coherent L1₂-type precipitates act as a structural mediator that (i) raise thermal conductivity, (ii) pin transformation strains, and (iii) supply abundant nucleation sites, thereby cutting magnetic/thermal hysteresis below 1 K while preserving >1 GPa strength. The magnitude of the isothermal entropy change |ΔS| and adiabatic temperature change ΔT_ad at μ₀H ≤ 0.5 T scale sharply with proximity to the critical VEC; a ±0.2 e⁄atom deviation halves |ΔS| and ΔT_ad.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic Fe–Mn–Co–Ni–Si high-entropy alloy processed by arc melting, homogenised (1200 °C/24 h, Ar) and water-quenched, followed by ageing at 600 °C/2 h to introduce 10–12 vol % coherent L1₂ nanoprecipitates in a bcc matrix (grain size ~20 µm). VEC ≈ 7.40 e⁄atom.
generation.intervention: Chemically substitute 2 at.% Mn with 2 at.% Fe (Fe₀.₂↑, Mn₀.₂↓) to increase VEC from 7.40 to 7.60 e⁄atom, holding processing, grain size and precipitate volume fraction identical.
generation.conditions: Magnetocaloric measurements between 150–400 K under μ₀H up to 0.5 T; tensile tests at 298 K; thermal conductivity by laser flash at 298 K.
generation.structural_mediator: 5–20 nm coherent L1₂ (Ni₃Si-type) nanoprecipitates homogeneously embedded in the bcc matrix.
generation.mechanism: At VEC ≈ 7.40 the electronic density of states peaks at E_F, lowering the energy barrier between paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases and producing a sharp first-order transition with large ΔM/ΔS under small fields. Nanoprecipitates improve heat transport and mechanically stabilise the lattice, reducing internal friction and arrest during cycling, which minimises hysteresis. Shifting VEC to 7.60 moves the Fermi level off the peak, making the transition second-order-like, broadening it, reducing ΔM, and thus lowering |ΔS| and ΔT_ad while leaving thermal and mechanical properties largely unchanged.
generation.predicted_outcome:
Relative to the baseline alloy (VEC = 7.40):
• |ΔS| at 0.5 T drops from ~5 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ to ≤ 2.5 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.
• ΔT_ad at 0.5 T drops from ~3 K to ≤ 1.5 K.
• Magnetic/thermal hysteresis width changes little (≤ 0.5 K difference).
• Room-temperature thermal conductivity and 0.2%-yield strength remain within ±10 % of baseline.
generation.baseline: Same alloy chemistry with VEC = 7.40, showing |ΔS| ≈ 5 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and ΔT_ad ≈ 3 K at μ₀H = 0.5 T, hysteresis < 1 K, thermal conductivity ~18 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, yield strength ~1.1 GPa.
generation.boundary: Hypothesis expected to hold for Fe–Mn–Co–Ni–Si (and minor Al, Cr) HEAs processed to retain a single bcc matrix with 5–20 nm coherent precipitates; temperature window 200–350 K; magnetic fields ≤ 1 T; VEC between 7.2 and 7.6 e⁄atom.
generation.uncertainty: No direct experimental map of VEC vs. MCE exists for this HEA family; magnitude changes (factor of two) are estimates. Precipitate coherence loss or texture development during processing could confound results. Electronic-structure peak location inferred from DFT trends, not measured.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three alloys: (A) baseline VEC = 7.40, (B) VEC = 7.60 (Mn→Fe), (C) VEC = 7.20 (Fe→Mn). Process all identically to create equivalent precipitate fractions. Measure (i) magnetisation vs. T at μ₀H = 0–0.5 T, (ii) ΔS (Maxwell relation) and ΔT_ad (direct) across 200–350 K, (iii) magnetic hysteresis (ΔT between heating/cooling peaks), (iv) thermal conductivity, (v) microhardness/yield strength.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If either substituted alloy (B or C) shows |ΔS| and ΔT_ad within ±15 % of the baseline values at 0.5 T while having the same low hysteresis and similar mechanical/thermal properties, the hypothesis is falsified; large MCE would then not be governed predominantly by proximity to VEC ≈ 7.40.
